messages:
sasha: Quick question about /rerank semantics — if an item in the request has no `score` field or it is `null`, what guarantees do we offer for ordering? do we treat it as -inf, 0, or fall back to stable input order?

josh: Short answer: we currently fall back to input order and then apply a deterministic tie-hash for server-side ordering. that tie-hash is internal (sha1(item_id) % 2^64). not exposed. :thinking_face:

maria: Follow up: that means clients that don't include stable ids (just text blobs) might see reorders between requests if client array ordering differs, right?

josh: correct. if client doesn't provide an `id` we use the array index as the tie key. so stable only if client preserves the same array order every time.

sanmay: Is the tie-hash behaviour documented anywhere? customers keep asking because some search UIs expect deterministic stable sort across retries.

josh: Not formally documented. There's an open RFC in the rerank repo but no public API contract. we should add a small section in the API docs: recommended to provide `id` for deterministic tie-breaking.

sasha: Another nuance — how do we treat `score: null` vs `score` missing? any difference in semantics?

maria: That came up in a bug yesterday. server treats both as "no score provided" and falls into fallback branch. code snippet:

```
// pseudocode
if (item.score is number) use it
else mark as unscored -> fallback to input-order + tie_hash
```
\nanna: what about score normalization? some models output logits vs probabilities; does rerank normalize before comparing?

josh: rerank does NOT normalize model logits. it expects callers to supply comparable scores (or use our model adapters which map to a common scale). mixing scales will break semantics. we should call this out in the contract.

sanmay: For backward compatibility: if we change tie-breaker in future (e.g., use a server-wide stable-seed), we need a version flag so old clients still get previous behaviour. agree?

maria: strongly agree. let's add `tie_mode` enum in request: "tie_mode": "legacy|stable-seed|random" with default `legacy`. default keeps current behaviour.

sasha: That would be a breaking change if default changes. PR idea: add `tie_mode` as opt-in for now, and set `tie_seed` optional when `stable-seed` is chosen.

josh: I'm +1. small API sketch for request shape:

```
POST /rerank
{
  \"items\": [ {\"id\": \"123\", \"text\": \"...\", \"score\": 0.87}, {\"id\": \"124\", \"text\": \"...\"} ],
  \"tie_mode\": \"legacy\", // optional
  \"tie_seed\": \"optional-uuid\"
}
```

and response example:

```
{
  \"ranked\": [ {\"id\":\"123\",\"score\":0.87,\"rank\":1}, {\"id\":\"124\",\"score\":null,\"rank\":2} ],
  \"tie_metadata\": {\"mode\":\"legacy\"}
}
```

anna: tiny nit: include `rank` so clients that don't trust order can read explicit positions. also `score` can be null in response to signal unscored.

sanmay: action items: josh will open a docs PR adding a section on unscored items and tie behaviour; maria will add the `tie_mode` proposal to the API RFC and add a short test plan; sasha will ping product about whether to expose `tie_seed` in the enterprise private deploy.

ci-bot: deploy check passed for rerank-service (main) — all tests green :white_check_mark:

josh: I'll open the two PRs this afternoon and add a small unit test ensuring `score: null` + missing-id uses input-order as documented. ping me if you want to pair.

sasha: thanks — leaving this thread open for async comments. @maria @sanmay please add your RFC links when ready. :memo:
